newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Chronology of events in Indo-Pakistan relations.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of events in Indo-Pakistan relations.

text.p: A chronology of major events between India and Pakistan, which plan to resume stalled peace talks on March 28-31 in New Delhi:
Oct 27, 1947: War breaks out between India and Pakistan in the disputed Himalayan region of Jammu and Kashmir, a little over two months after their independence from Britain.
Dec 31, 1948: Ceasefire, ordered by the United Nations Security Council, takes effect in Kashmir.
Sept 6-22, 1965: All-out India-Pakistan war over Kashmir, which ends after a U.N. call for ceasefire.
Jan 3, 1966: Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and Pakistani President Ayub Khan sign a Soviet-mediated peace pact at Tashkent, capital of Uzbekistan.
Dec 3-17, 1971: India-Pakistan war, during which Pakistani troops in East Pakistan (which later becomes Bangladesh) surrender on December 16.
July 2, 1972: Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Pakistani President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto sign peace accord at the Indian summer resort town of Simla.
Nov 1, 1982: Indira Gnadhi and Pakistan President Zia-ul-Haq agree to begin official discussions on non-agresssion treaty.
Dec 31, 1988: India and Pakistan sign agreement not to attack each other's nuclear facilities.

July 16-17, 1989: Indian Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi pays two-day visit to Pakistan during which he and Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto clash publicly over Kashmir and Islamabad's nuclear programme.

Jan 3, 1994: Foreign ministry secretaries of India and Pakistan fail to narrow differences on Kashmir, and Islamabad says no further talks can be held unless New Delhi reduces alleged human rights violations in Kashmir.
Dec 26, 1994: Pakistan orders closure of Indian consulate-general in Karachi, accusing it of involvement in acts of terrorism in Karachi. India rejects the charge.
Jan 4, 1995: India closes its consulate-general in Karachi.

Feb 17, 1997: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, in a letter to Pakistani counterpart Nawaz Sharif, congratulates him on taking office, proposes resumption of talks on a wide range of issues, including Kashmir.

Feb 27, 1997: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif agrees to resume talks with India and proposes that foreign ministry secretaries of the two countries meet before the end of March to prepare for a prime ministerial meeting.
March 6: India and Pakistan set March 28-31 for talks between their foreign ministry secretaries in New Delhi.
